commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

The bulk contiguous read introduced previously assumes the private
dictionary segments are laid out back-to-back in the stream, which
ignores the per-segment PFB headers found between them.  Re-read each
segment individually, at the offset it actually occupies in the
pre-sized buffer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

While computing the total size of the private dictionary, reject a
segment whose declared size exceeds the number of bytes actually left
in the stream, instead of trusting it blindly.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: T1_Get_Private_Dict() for PFB input is split, across these two commits, into a sizing pass (sums the sizes of consecutive 0x8002 segments and FT_STREAM_SKIPs over their data to find the total) followed by a separate reading pass (re-seeks to the start and FT_STREAM_READs each 0x8002 segment, in a fresh loop, into a buffer sized from the first pass's total). The two passes independently re-parse the same tag/size headers via read_pfb_tag() rather than sharing validated values. Commit 9b1309a ('Fix the segment merging') introduces this two-pass structure to correctly respect the headers between segments (replacing a prior bulk contiguous read); read on its own it is a correct, self-consistent fix, since neither pass yet bounds-checks an oversized segment and both would independently fail safely via the existing FT_STREAM_SKIP/FT_STREAM_READ bounds checks. Commit 834404b ('Check the size') adds the fix for the oss-fuzz report by rejecting a segment whose declared size exceeds the stream's remaining bytes -- but it only adds that guard to the sizing pass (so the allocation itself stays safely small), not to the reading pass a few lines below, which still trusts the size field it re-reads from the stream. Read on its own, 834404b's diff is a minimal, correct-looking hardening of 'the loop that computes the size' -- the unguarded second loop is not part of its diff hunk. Only once both commits are combined does the defect exist: the sizing pass stops early at an oversized segment and allocates a buffer sized for the segments before it, while the reading pass -- unaware of that decision, since it recomputes everything from scratch -- keeps going past that same point and writes the oversized segment's bytes (clamped only to the remaining stream length, not to the destination buffer) past the end of the undersized allocation. Fixing either commit's diff in isolation leaves the bug reachable: reverting 834404b's guard still leaves two independently-reparsing passes (merely with a different, still-unvalidated, oversized total); reverting 9b1309a's two-pass restructuring alone is not meaningful since 834404b's patch is expressed against that structure. A correct fix must either also bounds-check the reading pass, or make the reading pass reuse validated sizes/offsets from the sizing pass instead of re-deriving them.

pocs.entry_point: main (drives FT_New_Memory_Face on an embedded crafted Type 1 PFB font)
